items.title: Recoverable pipeline understated by $64,248
items.body: Part 1 headlines ≈$142.8K. Summing the per-account figures Part 1 itself prints ($26,388 + $64,248 + $27,444.72 + $20,000 + $24,000 + $25,000 + $20,000 + $0) gives $207,080.72. The $64,248 Home Lumber deal (closed Jul 25, 2025) is counted in that account's card and its "~$90K" note, but excluded from every stated total — both stat cards and the manager takeaways. True recoverable ≈ $207.1K, not ≈$142.8K.

items.title: The ownership gap is already closed
items.body: Part 1 shows five accounts as — assign, unowned. As of today HubSpot has all seven owned: Pouyan Mirsaeidi (Home Lumber, Southern Tool, Randy's Hardware, Handy Ace Hardware) and Joshua Kolenda (Gold Beach Lumber, Family Hardware, KB Home Center). Assigned after the July 21, 2026 match date used in Part 1. "Close the ownership gap" is done — don't send Josh and Pouyan chasing a solved problem at the booth.

items.title: Three accounts flagged "Not in ICP" — one is a hard blocker
items.body: Southern Tool Supply, Family Hardware, and KB Home Center all carry a rep-applied "Not in ICP" reason. KB Home Center's own lost-reason note is explicit: "not in ICP - Adyen no[t] supported in Turks & Caicos" — a payments-rail limitation, not a sales objection. Unless Adyen's Turks & Caicos coverage has changed, this account can't close regardless of the booth conversation. Recommend Skip alongside Mountain Mojo rather than #6 in the priority order, but this is a re-ranking call for the sales manager, not made here.

resolved.label: Both 2025 lost reasons
